title: Parallel-plate Flow Chamber and Continuous Flow Circuit to Evaluate Endothelial Progenitor Cells under Laminar Flow Shear Stress
protocol: Submit your research protocol to the Institutional Review Board (IRB).
Obtain informed consent from volunteer donors for peripheral blood collection and EPC isolation.
Collect 50 ml of peripheral blood via standard phlebotomy technique from a consented donor into anticoagulant-filled blood collection bags.
Dilute the collected blood solution 1:1 with Hank's buffered salt solution (without CaCl2, MgCl2, MgSO4).
Layer the diluted blood solution on equal volumes of Histopaque to create well-defined layers.
Centrifuge the sample for 30 minutes at 740 g with a low break setting.
Collect the mononuclear cell (MNC) layer from the buffy coat.
Resuspend and wash MNCs three times with Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffered Saline (DPBS) containing 10% Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS).
Wash each time for 10 minutes at 515 g.
Plate the resuspended MNCs into two 12-well plates in full EPC growth medium.
Culture the cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Change the medium every 24 hours for the first 7 days, then change it every other day.
Identify EPC colonies after an average of 14 days based on cobblestone morphology.
Once EPCs cover a quarter of the 12-well surface area, expand cells and confirm their identity with flow cytometry by testing for CD31 presence and absence of CD14 and CD45.
Expand isolated EPCs until they are nearly confluent in three T-75 cell culture flasks in EPC medium at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Cut the top and bottom plates of the chamber from aluminum alloy 6061 rectangular stock with top dimension of 7 x 2 x 0.5" and bottom dimensions of 7 x 2 x 0.25".
Recess the top plate in the center portion to 0.125" deep, leaving 0.950" per end for a fluid reservoir.
Drill 1/16" wide x 0.625" long slots from the underside to penetrate the inflow and outflow ends of the fluid reservoir.
At each end of the top plate, drill a centrally located 10/32" tracks per inch hole for polypropylene 1/8" hose barb to penetrate the fluid reservoir.
Create a side plug with a 10/32" T.P.I through hole for polypropylene 1/8" hose barb at the inflow end.
Taper the top underside from the fluid inflow to the glass viewing window at 0.518 degrees for adequate mixing of fluid.
Cut a glass slide window into the bottom plate in line with the top viewing window.
Glue a glass slide into the chamber using aquarium cement.
Allow the assembly to cure for at least 24 hours.
Ensure that the viewing window is recessed to accommodate a 75 x 25 x 1 mm microscope glass slide flush within the chamber.
Create a recess around the underside of the top and bottom plates for an O-ring, ensuring they are spaced apart by 0.02".
Insert rubber O-rings into place.
Drill 10 matching 8/32" T.P.I. holes in both the top and bottom chambers for use with 8/32" flat head screws.
Assemble the entire flow circuit before sterilizing it.
Attach a 36-inch segment of hard tubing to one end of the pulse dampener via a 1/8-inch connection.
Connect an 18-inch segment of soft tubing to the other end of the pulse dampener.
Place a 1/8-inch male luer adaptor at the end of the 18-inch soft tubing section.
Attach the male luer to a 1/8-inch female luer adaptor.
Connect the female luer to another new 18-inch segment of soft tubing.
Drill three holes into a 250 ml glass beaker cap for tubing placement.
Insert a 1.5-inch segment of soft tubing as an air vent through one hole in the cap.
Thread the free ends of both hard and soft tubing sections through the remaining two holes in the cap and into the 250 ml glass bottle (as reservoir).
Ensure that the hard tubing reaches to the bottom of the reservoir for proper outflow.
Sterilize parts by steam autoclaving at 121 °C for 60 min.

Autoclave one complete flow chamber, three 2-inch segments of soft tubing, one male and one female 1/8-inch luer adaptor, four ½-inch and six 5/16-inch 8-32 flat head screws, one pair of tweezers, one 75 x 25 x 1 mm glass slide, and two surgical towels.
Place sterile towels into laminar flow hood.
Place the flow circuit, flow chamber, four 4-way stopcocks, one 1-way stopcock, and all sterilized parts onto the sterile field.
Connect two 4-way stopcocks using sterile gloves.
Cap open sample ports.
Detach male and female luer adaptors from soft tubing segments of the flow circuit.
Insert connected stopcocks into detached ends of tubing.
Attach one end of soft tubing to a 30 ml syringe.
Remove syringe piston.
Fill bottle with 125 ml of EPC medium.
Place sterile syringe filter into air vent.
Move flow circuit into humidified incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.
Clamp hard tubing into roller pump head according to type of tubing.
Mark tubing where it exits the pump head on either side with a marking pen.
Ensure that all stopcocks are closed off towards the sample ports and open along the flow circuit.
Start the pump.
Verify the direction of flow.
Create a 1 mM stock solution of Cell Tracker Orange (CTO) by diluting 50 μg CTO powder with 90 μl of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Shield this mixture from light exposure.
Create a 2 μM working solution of CTO by diluting 36 μl of CTO stock solution into 18 ml of serum-free MCDB-131 medium.
Rinse EPCs in 3 near confluent T-75 cell culture flasks with 10 ml DPBS (without Ca or Mg).
Add 6 ml of the 2 μM CTO working solution to each flask.
Incubate for 15 min at 37 °C.
Rinse each flask x 2 with 10 ml DPBS (without Ca or Mg).
Add 4 ml of Trypsin to each flask.
Incubate at 37 °C for 3 min.
Neutralize with 8 ml of Trypsin Neutralization Solution.
Wash by centrifugation x 5 min at 600g.
Resuspend in 5 ml of EPC medium.
Place the slide into a sterile rectangular four-chamber cell culture vessel.
Count cells and seed 1.5 x 10^6 cells onto the slide in 5 ml of EPC medium for 6 hours if a confluent cell layer is desired at initiation of flow.
Allow 3 x 10^6 cells to adhere for only 15 minutes before commencement of flow to test cell spreading and adhesion under fluid shear stress.
Connect one 2" soft tubing segment to a 1/8" female luer adaptor.
Connect another 2" soft tubing segment to a 1/8" male luer adaptor.
Attach the 2" soft tubing with female luer adaptor to the inflow port.
Attach the 2" soft tubing with male luer to the outflow port.
Attach 4-way stopcocks to both of these luer adaptors.
Connect the remaining 2" soft tubing piece to the side port connector coming off the bubble trap and attach a 1-way stopcock.
Using sterile tweezers, remove the cell-seeded slide from the cell culture vessel.
Place the cell-seeded slide into the recess on the bottom plate of the flow chamber with the cell-seeded side facing up.
Pipette 10 ml of warm EPC medium onto the slide.
Allow the medium to cover the slide and flow chamber, but do not spill over the O-ring on the bottom plate.
Place the top plate of the flow chamber onto the bottom plate, aligning the screw holes.
Screw plates together (an automatic battery-operated screwdriver speeds up this process).
Remove air bubbles from inflow bubble trap by opening the 1-way stopcock attached to the inflow-side bubble trap port and gently flush with EPC medium using a 10 ml syringe.
Close off the stopcock and cap it.
Open the outflow port 4-way stopcock to remove air bubbles from the chamber channel.
Gently flush EPC medium through the flow chamber, again using a 10 ml syringe.
Raise the outflow end of the chamber to a 45° angle if large bubbles remain.
Cap all of the 4-way stopcock connections and close them off.
Move the flow chamber into the incubator with the assembled flow circuit.
Pause the flow circuit pump.
Close off the flow circuit stopcocks in the direction of flow to prevent leakage.
Transport the flow chamber from the flow hood to the flow circuit.
Connect the flow chamber to the flow circuit.
Open the stopcocks in the direction of flow.
Resume the flow pump.
Ensure that the perfusate flows in the correct direction.
Adjust the flow rate to the desired shear stress.
Disconnect the flow chamber from the flow circuit at the stopcock-stopcock connections for imaging.
Close off the flow circuit stopcocks and flow chamber stopcocks in the direction of flow during removal.
Cap all stopcocks prior to removing the flow circuit from the incubator.
Pause the pump for perfusate sample collection.
Close the stopcock located closest to the pulse dampener.
Remove its protective cap and insert a small size syringe into the sample port.
Keep the cap upside down to avoid contamination.
Close the stopcock in the direction of the flow chamber.
Draw 150 μl of sample from the circuit.
Close off the stopcock towards the sample port before removing the syringe.
Store the perfusate sample in a labeled vial and freeze at -80°C.
Recap the sample port.
Ensure that all stopcocks are open before commencing flow.
